stem_lines: A phone manufacturer's records over many thousands of phones show that 3% have a defective screen. A store receives a random shipment of 200 phones. The store manager says, "Since 3% are defective, exactly 6 phones in this shipment will have a defective screen." Which statement best evaluates the manager's claim?

choices.t: The claim is correct, because 3% of 200 is 6.
The claim is incorrect, because the manager should have used 97%, since most phones in the shipment are not defective.
The claim is incorrect, because a probability describes the long-run proportion, so the number of defective phones in this particular shipment will vary around 6 and need not equal 6.
The claim is incorrect, because a 3% rate applies only to shipments of 1,000 or more phones.

notes: Rationales: A: confuses an expected count with a guaranteed one. B: confuses the event with its complement. D: invents a minimum sample size; probability applies to each phone.

stem_lines: For two events A and B, P(A) = 0.50, P(B) = 0.30, and P(A or B) = 0.65. Which statement is correct?

choices.t: A and B are mutually exclusive, because P(A or B) = 0.65 is less than 1.
A and B are both mutually exclusive and independent, because P(A and B) equals P(A)P(B).
A and B are neither mutually exclusive nor independent, because P(A or B) ≠ P(A) + P(B).
A and B are not mutually exclusive, because P(A and B) = 0.15 > 0, but they are independent, because 0.15 = (0.50)(0.30).

notes: Rationales: A: a union below 1 says nothing about overlap. B: mutually exclusive events with positive probabilities can never be independent. C: unequal sum shows overlap, not dependence.

Athlete, On honor roll: 24

Which statement is correct?

choices.t: Being an athlete and being on the honor roll are not independent, because more non-athletes (36) than athletes (24) are on the honor roll.
Being an athlete and being on the honor roll are not independent, because P(athlete | honor roll) = 0.40 is not equal to P(honor roll | athlete) = 0.30.
Being an athlete and being on the honor roll are independent, because P(honor roll | athlete) = 24/80 = 0.30 equals P(honor roll) = 60/200 = 0.30.
Being an athlete and being on the honor roll are independent, because P(athlete and honor roll) = 0.12 is smaller than both P(athlete) and P(honor roll).

notes: Rationales: A: compares counts of unequal groups. B: P(A | B) and P(B | A) are different quantities; they need not be equal. D: a joint probability is always smaller than each marginal; it does not show independence.

notes: Check: SD of x̄ = 12/√36 = 2; z = (53 − 50)/2 = 1.5; P(Z > 1.5) = 0.0668. A: used σ = 12, z = 0.25, a probability about one individual. B: P(Z < 1.5), the wrong tail. C: doubled to a two-sided area.

stem_lines: A population of delivery times has standard deviation 20 minutes. A researcher takes random samples and computes the sample mean. When the sample size is 25, the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of x̄ is 4 minutes. If the sample size is increased to 100, which statement is correct?

choices.t: The standard deviation of x̄ decreases from 4 to 1, because four times as many observations make it one-fourth as large.
The standard deviation of x̄ decreases from 4 to 2, because it is proportional to 1/√n.
The standard deviation of x̄ stays at 4, because the population standard deviation is still 20.
The standard deviation of x̄ increases, because a larger sample has more observations that can vary.

notes: Check: SD ∝ 1/√n; 1/3 requires √n × 3, so n × 9. A: forgot the square root. D: cubed.
